title: An electronic nose and neural network classified berry ripeness grades
summary: An electronic nose and a three-layer neural network classified five expert-assigned ripeness grades in whiteberries and blackberries. The paper reports 100% correct classification for blackberries and 88.3% for whiteberries, with overlap between the last two whiteberry grades. The result comes from a small internal sample and does not establish performance across harvests or sites.
organization: Razi University; University of Tehran; Agricultural Science and Natural Resources University of Khuzestan

evidence.tested: The study used 120 fruits and a 75/25 training/test split.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: The ANN classified sensor patterns into expert-assigned ripeness grades.

source_review.scope: Read the original full text, including author affiliations, Methods and Results; checked the first result-bearing version and active/archive catalog for same-result records.
